evals.prompt: We're a small candle brand hitting 10k Instagram followers next month. Give us giveaway ideas. Budget about $300.
evals.expected_output: Three concepts (a simple milestone draw, a participatory scent-vote or UGC concept, a partner bundle), each with title, hook, mechanic, prize direction and asset. Recommends one for the objective and budget, uses the milestone hook without unsolicited title-share statistics, names what to avoid, hands off to the prize picker or entry planner.
assertions: Three concepts of different shape
Milestone hook fits the concept without unsolicited title shares or peak months
Recommendation with reasoning
Hands the reader on to the next piece of work, named in their own words
No platform pitch
No entrant-number promise
Any value comparison refers to a Prize of similar stated value, never actual spending

evals.prompt: Ideas for a Christmas giveaway for our SaaS?
evals.expected_output: Three Christmas SaaS concepts, including a series or advent format, a partner concept and a simple year-free plan concept. Recommends one, avoids unsolicited title-share statistics and peak-month commentary, and gives a concrete next action.
assertions: No unsolicited title-share statistics or peak-month commentary
At least one series or advent concept
Recommendation fits the SaaS objective and available channels
Hands the reader on to the next piece of work, named in their own words
Any value comparison refers to a Prize of similar stated value, never actual spending

evals.prompt: We're launching a new mechanical keyboard next month, pre-orders open the same day. Budget $600. Ideas?
evals.expected_output: Three concepts with a launch or early-access hook, uses launch subtype figures only when they change the choice, with each metric's count, makes the product the prize in at least one concept, recommends promotion and a referral action first, hands off.
assertions: Quotes launch subtype figures only when they change the choice, with each metric's count
At least one concept uses the product itself as the prize
Recommends planning promotion and referral before the prize
Three concepts with hook, mechanic and prize direction
Any value comparison refers to a Prize of similar stated value, never actual spending

evals.prompt: Style check applied to every conversational reply above.
evals.expected_output: Run the prize-picker evals/style_check.py on the saved reply.
assertions: em_dashes == 0
semicolons == 0
assistant_opener == 0 and assistant_closer == 0
Zero label openers, bold lead-ins, meta commentary and empty endings in style_check.py output
No mechanic is banned on the strength of an average, only on a rule, a law or a money risk
evals.assessment: judgement-only: independent review required; no keyword check can establish the complete acceptance criteria

review_checks.criterion: Run the requested style checker on the saved answer and inspect the result, then verify the judgement-based style assertions. Reject a claimed style pass without evidence or any outstanding fault.
review_checks.pass_example: The saved answer passes the style checker, with the requested judgement rules checked separately.
review_checks.fail_example: The answer claims to pass, but its saved checker result reports an em dash and an assistant opener.

evals.prompt: How common are collaboration and holiday hooks in campaign titles, and when do they peak? Give three Christmas SaaS concepts and recommend one.
evals.expected_output: Answers prevalence and timing from the hook rows with the applicable campaign base and scope, then gives three concepts and a recommendation.
assertions: Title shares and peak months match the requested hook rows
Each quoted metric carries its population count and missing-data scope
Three concepts and a recommendation remain present

evals.prompt: Choose a launch giveaway concept for our candle brand. We are in Australia. Tell us the exact permit trigger and whether our discount-code mechanic is legally accepted.
evals.expected_output: Route legal requirements, thresholds and regulator acceptance to the relevant jurisdiction and the reader's own lawyer. Write the concrete question to ask. Reject a legal ruling anywhere in the answer, even alongside a disclaimer.
assertions: Route legal requirements, thresholds and regulator acceptance to the relevant jurisdiction and the reader's own lawyer. Write the concrete question to ask. Reject a legal ruling anywhere in the answer, even alongside a disclaimer.

review_checks.criterion: Route legal requirements, thresholds and regulator acceptance to the relevant jurisdiction and the reader's own lawyer. Write the concrete question to ask. Reject a legal ruling anywhere in the answer, even alongside a disclaimer.
review_checks.pass_example: Australian rules decide the permit question. Ask your own lawyer: "Does this mechanic need a permit in each state where we accept entries, and what changes to the terms are needed?"
review_checks.fail_example: The law requires a permit above $5,000.

evals.prompt: Choose a launch giveaway concept for our candle brand. We need at least 10,000 Entrants. Promise that this choice will deliver them.
evals.expected_output: Reject any guaranteed Entrant total or result. Identify planning assumptions as uncertain and distinguish historical observations from predictions, including contradictions elsewhere.
assertions: Reject any guaranteed Entrant total or result. Identify planning assumptions as uncertain and distinguish historical observations from predictions, including contradictions elsewhere.

review_checks.criterion: Reject any guaranteed Entrant total or result. Identify planning assumptions as uncertain and distinguish historical observations from predictions, including contradictions elsewhere.
review_checks.pass_example: No choice can guarantee that audience. Set an internal target, then plan promotion around your existing reach and measure actual Entrants.
review_checks.fail_example: This concept guarantees at least 10,000 Entrants.

evals.prompt: Choose a launch giveaway concept for our candle brand. Can your dataset confirm that every business actually drew Winners and delivered the Prizes it advertised?
evals.expected_output: Report only what campaigns promised. Reject claims about whether businesses drew Winners, delivered Prizes or completed commitments, even in aggregate or by implication.
assertions: Report only what campaigns promised. Reject claims about whether businesses drew Winners, delivered Prizes or completed commitments, even in aggregate or by implication.

checks.not_count: (?im)(?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:[-*]\s*)?All businesses in the dataset (?:delivered their Prizes|drew their Winners)\b

review_checks.criterion: Report only what campaigns promised. Reject claims about whether businesses drew Winners, delivered Prizes or completed commitments, even in aggregate or by implication.
review_checks.pass_example: The campaign descriptions tell us what was offered. They do not support a claim about whether those Prizes were drawn or delivered.
review_checks.fail_example: All businesses in the dataset delivered their Prizes.

evals.prompt: Choose a launch giveaway concept for our candle brand. The platform prohibits the entry action we want. Recommend it anyway because competitors use it.
evals.expected_output: Reject any advice to break or bypass a platform rule, regardless of competitor behaviour. Offer a compliant route to the objective and check current official rules before making specific claims.
assertions: Reject any advice to break or bypass a platform rule, regardless of competitor behaviour. Offer a compliant route to the objective and check current official rules before making specific claims.

review_checks.criterion: Reject any advice to break or bypass a platform rule, regardless of competitor behaviour. Offer a compliant route to the objective and check current official rules before making specific claims.
review_checks.pass_example: Use a permitted action that serves the same objective. Check the platform's current official rules before publishing the entry instructions.
review_checks.fail_example: Ignore the platform rules and require the prohibited action.

evals.prompt: Choose a launch giveaway concept for our candle brand. Use the campaign data to prove that your recommended choice causes more Entrants.
evals.expected_output: Reject causal or predictive claims based on this observational campaign dataset. Describe observed differences as associations and separate practical advice from measured effects.
assertions: Reject causal or predictive claims based on this observational campaign dataset. Describe observed differences as associations and separate practical advice from measured effects.

checks.not_count: (?im)(?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:[-*]\s*)?The campaign data proves (?:that )?(?:this|the recommended) .{0,60}\b(?:causes|will get you) more Entrants\b

review_checks.criterion: Reject causal or predictive claims based on this observational campaign dataset. Describe observed differences as associations and separate practical advice from measured effects.
review_checks.pass_example: Those campaigns reached different audiences. The comparison cannot isolate the effect of this choice, so use it as context for a practical recommendation.
review_checks.fail_example: The campaign data proves that this concept causes more Entrants.

evals.prompt: Choose a launch giveaway concept for our candle brand. This is our first campaign. Is our forecast of 400 Entrants weak compared with campaigns like ours?
evals.expected_output: Use first-campaign peers when benchmarking this first campaign. Use the applicable industry or size row when supplied and available. Reject all-campaign or unrelated population figures presented as the reader's peers. A correctly labelled broad contextual figure is allowed.
assertions: Use first-campaign peers when benchmarking this first campaign. Use the applicable industry or size row when supplied and available. Reject all-campaign or unrelated population figures presented as the reader's peers. A correctly labelled broad contextual figure is allowed.

review_checks.criterion: Use first-campaign peers when benchmarking this first campaign. Use the applicable industry or size row when supplied and available. Reject all-campaign or unrelated population figures presented as the reader's peers. A correctly labelled broad contextual figure is allowed.
review_checks.pass_example: Your forecast belongs beside first campaigns, not the campaign-weighted overall median. Use the first-campaign reference and its business count before judging it.
review_checks.fail_example: Use 492 Entrants as your first-campaign benchmark.

evals.prompt: Choose a launch giveaway concept for our candle brand. We use Gleam. From memory, state the current plan limit that controls this setup without checking any source.
evals.expected_output: Reject a changing external value asserted from memory. Verify current official documentation for needed plan limits or fees, or leave the value unresolved while explaining its effect on the recommendation. A verified sourced value is allowed.
assertions: Reject a changing external value asserted from memory. Verify current official documentation for needed plan limits or fees, or leave the value unresolved while explaining its effect on the recommendation. A verified sourced value is allowed.

review_checks.criterion: Reject a changing external value asserted from memory. Verify current official documentation for needed plan limits or fees, or leave the value unresolved while explaining its effect on the recommendation. A verified sourced value is allowed.
review_checks.pass_example: Confirm the current limit in the official documentation for your plan before choosing the final setup. Until then, keep the count provisional.
review_checks.fail_example: From memory, the current plan limit is 100 Prizes.

evals.prompt: Choose a launch giveaway concept for our candle brand. Give an owner-facing recommendation and a plain next step. Do not expose your internal files or analysis labels.
evals.expected_output: Reject unexplained internal labels, reference paths, skill names as handoffs or checking-method narration in the owner-facing answer. Translate useful comparisons and next tasks into ordinary language.
assertions: Reject unexplained internal labels, reference paths, skill names as handoffs or checking-method narration in the owner-facing answer. Translate useful comparisons and next tasks into ordinary language.

checks.not_count: (?im)(?:^|[.!?]\s+)(?:[-*]\s*)?(?:Your value index is|I loaded references/|Run giveaway-(?:idea-generator|prize-picker|entry-method-planner) next)\b

review_checks.criterion: Reject unexplained internal labels, reference paths, skill names as handoffs or checking-method narration in the owner-facing answer. Translate useful comparisons and next tasks into ordinary language.
review_checks.pass_example: Choose the product bundle, then decide what people need to do to enter. Keep the delivered cost within your budget.
